sourceAuthority: docs/SPEC.md eprint writes supplied Text bytes without switching streams; print/println likewise retain the supplied length and platform line policy.
differences: CSharp direct stdout truncates to i32. SLG both normal and parallel-direct stdout paths and eprint also truncate.
CSharp stderr imposes Int32 length ceiling and accepts only a single complete write. SLG stderr already reuses a loop but its length is truncated before the loop.
CSharp stdout has a per-call written pointer and cached console mode; SLG uses a single global count and queries console mode per helper.
SLG computes buffered count+len before checking the buffer limit; CSharp excludes oversized input first.
decision: Share identical generated write_stream_chunk and write_stream bodies. Keep length and offset64 and cap each chunk to1MiB.
Only console chunks retreat at most3 UTF8 continuation bytes at a split. Redirected bytes are unrestricted; preserve invalid UTF8 failure on console.
Retain positive/bounded partial-write checks and heap cleanup through shared chunk helper, with a private per-call count pointer.
Use existing stream choice and newline wrappers. Route both SLG direct-output branches and stderr through a full-width wrapper.
Use len<=bufferAvailable in the SLG buffered predicate, so wrapped count+len cannot admit an oversized copy.
contractNotes: Private UInt32 written slot reports the most recent bounded chunk; public output callers inspect success, not that slot as an aggregate UInt64 length.
Captured memory output already carries the full UInt64 byte length; its old diagnostic UInt32 truncation does not truncate the captured bytes. No change to this path.
Console test uses actual Windows UTF8 conversion and heap APIs with simulated full/partial console writes; no interactive-console or huge real IO claim.
remainingGates: Existing parallel output callback controls and source route checks for both capture variants
All original final whole, Stage, stdlib/runtime, platform/performance gates
